body:
NX8's 8-bit static formats lose most on div outputs: microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition keeps only -inf dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) there even in its best format (fp8_e3m4). Measured on 37 models with a format search (of 666 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 22.1 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst -2.4 dB (Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B). 17 of 31 models with a labelled metric lose some of it; the most: jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (agreement -1), openai/whisper-base (agreement -1) and microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (agreement -1).

The tensors that lose most even in their best format: div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), linear in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors (fp8_e3m4, -19.0 dB), bmm in openai/whisper-small (fp8_e3m4, -15.0 dB), mul in openai/whisper-small (fp8_e3m4, -15.0 dB), bmm in Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (fp8_e2m5, -14.0 dB), linear in Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (fp8_e2m5, -13.8 dB), linear in EleutherAI/pythia-160m (fp8_e3m4, -12.1 dB), linear in Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (fp8_e2m5, -12.0 dB), bmm in Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (fp8_e2m5, -10.3 dB) and gelu in openai/whisper-small (fp8_e3m4, -9.8 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 12558 (51%), fp8_e3m4 8532 (35%), fp8_e1m6 2996 (12%), ufp8_e2m6 310 (1.26%), ufp8_e1m7 127 (0.52%), ufp8_e3m5 26 (0.11%), fp8_e4m3 1 (under 0.01%); 1.89% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where the most data carries the most error: div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB) and div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB).

6 missing capabilities keep 52 operations in 13 models (of 32 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (33 operations in 9 models). Ranked by the MACs they hold:

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding and gather) needs a workaround. It affects 33 operations in 9 models: 33 calls (0.31% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256, embedding in BAAI/bge-reranker-large and embedding in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions. Cost today: 1 of 33 have a workaround (1 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 32 wait for one; 231 workarounds proposed, 95 passing its check, 69 evaluated on a model; the workarounds lose no measurable accuracy (0.00 dB of model output SQNR, measured on 1 operation); cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**An upsample instruction.** The chip has no instruction for upsample, so every upsample needs a workaround. It affects 11 operations in 3 models: 11 calls (0.10% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: upsample in mattmdjaga/segformer_b2_clothes, upsample in nvidia/segformer-b2-finetuned-ade-512-512 and upsample in nvidia/segformer-b0-finetuned-ade-512-512. title: Missing instructions: 52 operations in 13 models need workarounds

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 847 of 1981 tensors passed between kernels (43%) in 28 models: 501 for attention heads split or merged, 311 for other reshapes, 17 for pixels reordered, 15 for dimensions merged and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 671 operations (671 calls, 6.20% of all calls; 131 G MACs, 3.68% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207, linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 203 and add → bmm (other reshapes) 80; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (208), Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (137) and stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (129).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 847 of 1981 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 2,473 operations in 30 models (2,473 calls, 23% of all calls), most often layernorm (693), silu (392) and softmax (389). Their quantized accuracy: worst -inf dB SQNR over 1,836 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 12.5, most 65 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 65 planned groups), over 32 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.1 powers of ten for bmm in Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (largest value 2.75e+05).

268 outputs in 12 models hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (246), select_where (19) and amin (2), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

2 accuracy runs produced non-finite outputs (overflow or NaN).

Instruction memory (IMEM, 1,024 words per bank) use: not measured yet (no kernel built).
title: Resource limits: 2,473 operations limited by the LUT and up to 65 kernel launches per pass

body: The most costly finding is the missing run-time addressing capability, which blocks 36 operations across 9 models (embedding/gather calls, data movement only) with no working workaround yet — 213 proposals exist but only 85 pass checks and none have measured accuracy or cycles. Next is quantisation loss: model outputs keep a median 22.1 dB SQNR against full precision (worst −2.4 dB), and 17 of 31 models with a labelled metric lose some of it, with division outputs in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition losing everything (−inf dB even in its best format, fp8_e3m4) and other worst tensors in linear, bmm, mul and gelu around −9.8 to −19.0 dB. Layout conversions are the third cost: 844 of 1,978 tensors between kernels (43%) must be rearranged by the reading kernel — mostly attention head splits/merges after linear layers — affecting 668 calls (6.18% of calls, 3.68% of MACs), though the extra cycles are not yet measured. Fourth, resource limits: 2,473 operations (23% of calls) go through the 256-entry LUT with worst-case −inf dB SQNR, forward passes need a median 12.5 kernel launches (up to 65 for stable-diffusion-v1-5), 268 outputs sit at the FP32 limit, and 2 accuracy runs produced non-finite outputs. Least costly are the remaining missing instructions — upsample (11 ops, 3 models), cumsum (3 ops, already fully worked around with 0.00 dB loss), and the single-op aten::type_as, aten::conv1d and aten::einsum cases (1 op each, no workaround passing yet) — while MAC utilisation and IMEM use are not measured at all.
title: GLM summary

body:
**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip)** would put 33 operations in 9 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 33 calls (0.31% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); recovering 0.00 dB of model output SQNR measured on 1 workaround.

**An upsample instruction** would put 11 operations in 3 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 11 calls (0.10% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**A cumsum instruction** would put 3 operations in 3 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 3 calls (0.03% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); recovering 0.00 dB of model output SQNR measured on 3 workarounds.

**An aten::type_as instruction** would put 3 operations in 3 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 3 calls (0.03% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**An aten::conv1d instruction** would put 1 operation in 1 model on the chip directly, with no workaround: 1 call (under 0.01% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**An aten::einsum instruction** would put 1 operation in 1 model on the chip directly, with no workaround: 1 call (under 0.01% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).
